authority.source: Proposed formalization; placeholder definitions await owner review.

scope: Declared ordered event observations; example definitions are placeholders.

trace.order: authoritative recorded event order, including rejections and retries
trace.projection: retain each recorded event without sorting, merging or deduplication
trace.model: placeholder composed model; execution membership is unproved
trace.environment: placeholder capabilities; no omitted actor is implicitly excluded
trace.initialization: separate initial-state check, including zero-operation executions
trace.continuity: requires post/pre correspondence at every retained boundary

assumptions.definition: PLACEHOLDER A: recording/execution continues, asset service remains available, and exit processing is weakly fair. A assumes neither completion nor alarm clearance. A finite non-resettable delay budget must independently establish persistent exit enablement.

A.definition: PLACEHOLDER A: recording/execution continues, asset service remains available, and exit processing is weakly fair. A assumes neither completion nor alarm clearance. A finite non-resettable delay budget must independently establish persistent exit enablement.

R.definition: PLACEHOLDER legitimacy is fixed at submission before acceptance; request identity is never reused and policy changes cannot erase it.

C.definition: PLACEHOLDER matching assets returned to the same frozen request identity; another request cannot witness completion.

readings.body: forall sigma in Traces: A(sigma) => (forall r in Requests: always(R(r) => eventually(C(r))))
readings.intuitive: provided A, every legitimate submitted withdrawal eventually returns its matching assets, even when alarms occur
readings.plain: provided A, an alarm may delay a withdrawal but never freeze it
